To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the throughput of an OLTP system can be modeled as a piecewise linear function of the ratio of read to write requests, and the number of active transactions; (2) the throughput can be predicted by using a linear regression model; and (3) the throughput can also be predicted by using the model of a single transaction, and the model of the number of active concurrent transactions, and by using a simple linear combination of these two models.

(a) the number of concurrent requests is the most important parameter for performance prediction, (b) the ratio of transactions to requests is the second most important parameter, and (c) the ratio of reads to writes is the third most important parameter.

1) OLTP workloads are not only characterized by high concurrency but also by a large number of transactions that are short-lived and exhibit complex interactions, and 2) the performance of an OLTP system depends on the characteristics of the transactions that are running in it, and the interactions between them, and is not solely a function of the hardware resources that the system uses.
